_doc: The declared CPU's cpuid, as DATA: the raw leaves of the pinned reference host (identity: verify/cpuref.json) and the declared-machine masks applied to them. lift/tools/gen_cpuref.py generates lift/rt/fnvl_cpuref.h, lift/rt/rcpref.h and lift/rt/cpumodel_tab.inc from cpuref.json + this file; nothing restates these values by hand. Provenance of `raw`: transcribed from the table recorded in lift/rt/cpumodel.c at 286fdc93 (a `cpuid` run on the pinned host). Fields the platform owns (leaf 1 EBX [23:16], leaf 4 EAX [31:26] and the L3 share field [25:14]) are zero in `raw` and filled by rt/cpumodel.c from FNVNX_NPROC.
mxcsr_mask_doc: DERIVED, no capture (orchestrator ruling 2026-11-15). Source: Intel SDM Vol 1 §11.6.6 (ASM-055, OWNER 10: the ISA as the SDM documents it) with CPUREF's identity row (verify/cpuref.json, family 6 model 207, a DAZ-capable part): its FXSAVE MXCSR_MASK is 0xFFFF. Restricted to the declared feature set (host ∩ lifted): DAZ (MXCSR bit 6) is outside the lifted set (no Form implements DAZ), so mxcsr_mask = 0xFFFF & ~0x40 = 0xFFBF. LDMXCSR of a value with a bit outside the mask is #GP(0) (SDM Vol 2 LDMXCSR, Exceptions).
masks_doc: leaf1 EDX = raw & ~clear: SS (27) cleared (kept HTT 28, FXSR SSE SSE2 ...); leaf1 ECX = raw & keep (everything cleared: the lifter implements MMX/SSE/SSE2 only); 0x80000001 EDX = raw & keep (NX only); ECX = raw & keep (LAHF64, LZCNT/ABM, PREFETCHW cleared). max leaves: a 2010-era game asks leaves 0 1 2 4 and 0x80000000..4.
capstone_groups_doc: The CPUID feature bit of every capstone x86 instruction group that names a CPU feature (capstone 5.0.7 x86_const X86_GRP_* of the lifter's pinned decoder; the totality test tests/test_cleared_groups.py checks that every X86_GRP_* constant is a key of capstone_groups or a member of capstone_nonfeature). Value: [leaf, register, bit]. An instruction that capstone tags with a group whose bit is 0 in the declared CPU's cpuid (the words of leaves 1 and 0x80000001 above; a leaf above max_basic / max_ext is all zero) is #UD (owner decision, CLAUDE.md 'The declared CPU'). Bit positions: Intel SDM Vol 2 Table 3-10 (leaf 1 ECX), Table 3-11 (leaf 1 EDX), Table 3-8 (leaf 7 EBX) and AMD APM Vol 3 Appendix E (0x80000001 EDX/ECX: 3DNow, SSE4A, XOP, FMA4, TBM).
exec_as_nop_doc: The encodings that a CPU WITHOUT the feature executes as NOP, one row per feature: [leaf, register, bit, [opcode byte pairs 0F xx (hex), the cells of the SDM opcode map that hold only that feature's instructions: lift/proof/tests/opmap_cells.tsv], the SDM citation]. An instruction at such an encoding whose CPUID bit is 0 on the declared CPU executes as NOP (a Form with no effect, no memory access and no fault); every other cleared feature is #UD (capstone_groups). Read by lift/proof/cpufeat.py nop(); no feature or opcode appears in the lifter.

MPX: Intel SDM Vol. 1, Appendix E.4.1 Instruction Encoding: 'All Intel MPX instructions are NOP on processors that report CPUID.07H.00H:EBX.MPX[14] = 0'

ud_encodings_doc: Encodings of a feature that the pinned decoder (capstone) gives NO feature group (capstone_groups has no row for them), one row per feature: [leaf, register, bit, [{op: opcode byte after the legacy prefixes, reg: the ModRM reg field, mem: true = memory form only}], the SDM citation of the #UD line]. An instruction at such an encoding whose CPUID bit is 0 on the declared CPU is #UD, like a capstone group (cpufeat.missing). The census of the gaps is lift/proof/udcensus.py.

SSE3_FISTTP: Intel SDM Vol. 2A, FISTTP: '#UD If CPUID.01H:ECX.SSE3[0] = 0.'
